description:
FOUND s438 (Opus 5) by the #473 census population (cpan-tests/modules/**/t/**/*.t).
That population carries 83 drops in 42 files, and SEVENTY-NINE of them are one
mechanism.

THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (two files, identical but for the package NAME):

  package Test2::Fake;  our @EXPORT = qw(blk);  sub blk (&) { $_[0]->() }
  package My::Blk2;     our @EXPORT = qw(blk);  sub blk (&) { $_[0]->() }

  use Test2::Fake;  my $r = blk { 42; };   -> PCL DROPS the statement
  use My::Blk2;     my $r = blk { 42; };   -> lowers and runs (r=42)

CAUSE, and it is deliberate-looking code: Pl::Parser::_extract_module_prototypes
(Pl/Parser.pm ~8410) returns undef for any module matching /^Test2::/ or
/^Test::/ except Test::More --

    # Skip the heavy Test2 stack and Test:: internals -- EXCEPT Test::More ...

so the `(&)` prototype is never read, the call is not a block-form call, and
the term grammar cannot lower `blk { ... };`.  The affected names in the census
are Test2's intercept (53), exception (8), capture (7), warnings (4),
no_context (3), context_do (2) and Text::CSV's try/async (2).

THE SECOND HALF IS SILENT, and it is the worse one: only a block whose body
ENDS IN A SEMICOLON drops.  `blk { 42 }` (no semicolon) parses as a hash-ish
argument and emits `(pl-blk 42)` -- the block's VALUE is passed where perl
passes a CODE REF.  Probed: perl prints 42, PCL dies at run time with an
unhandled condition.  So the same skip produces a drop in one spelling and a
wrong program in the other.

WHY THE SKIP EXISTS (read before removing it): Test::More resolves to PCL's own
tiny lib/Test/More.pm shim, whose prototypes (is($$;$), ok($;$), ...) impose
scalar context; the comment says the rest of the Test2 stack is "heavy" -- i.e.
the skip is a COMPILE-TIME cost measure, not a semantic one.  Measure that cost
before deciding: the prototype walk is one PPI parse per module, memoized, and
the s411 census already timed _premerge_include_prototypes (task #391).

ALSO A LAYER SMELL (CLAUDE.md 9a): the skip list names CPAN modules inside
Pl/Parser.pm.  Whatever the fix is, it should key on a MECHANISM (cost, depth,
a shim marker) rather than on more module names.

BAR: the 79 census rows leave docs/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv by EDIT;
a Pl/t guard for both spellings (drop and silent mis-parse) against a
locally-declared Test2::-named module; compile-time A/B over the corpus
(tools/corpus-diff.pl reports the time) because the skip is there for speed.
DONE s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5): THE NAME LIST IS GONE.  The ruled
BUDGET fallback was implemented, measured, and deliberately NOT shipped.

THE COST THE LIST WAS BUYING, measured over the cpan-t census population
(289 files, one pl2cl process each -- the population the list served):

    with the Test::/Test2:: skip     65.5 s    83 drops
    without it                      281.3 s    11 drops

So the correctness win is 72 of the 83 drops (the task's prediction of 79 was
close; the residue is #480/#481/#482 and friends), and the cost is real: 4.3x,
because `use Test2::API qw/intercept/` walks 27 modules / 242 KB of perl
through PPI and `state $cache` dies with the process.

THE BUDGET DOES NOT PAY, and this is the part worth not re-deriving.  A
depth-aware byte budget on the NESTED walks was implemented (own includes
always read; recursion capped; a cut ANNOUNCED, never silent) and measured:

    budget      289 files    40 files
    none         281.3 s      37.9 s
    128 KB          --        51.6 s   <- SLOWER than no budget
     32 KB       212.0 s      27.3 s
      0          162.4 s      23.8 s

Non-monotone, and the reason is structural: a TRUNCATED walk cannot go in the
process-wide memo, because caching it would make file 2's emission depend on
how much budget file 1 had left (`pl2cl --server` transpiles many files from
one process).  So a cut forces re-walks, and the more that is walked before
the cut the more is re-walked.  Only the extreme (own includes, never recurse)
was faster -- and that one breaks a genuine re-export chain: at 32 KB the ONE
perl-tests file that took a cut was tr.t, whose `use Encode` reaches
Encode::Alias / Encode::MIME::Name / Storable at depth 2.  Drops were 11 at
every budget, so the deep transitive tail buys no prototype this population
uses -- but no safe value exists that both avoids repo-population cuts and
saves time.

THE REAL FIX FOR THE COST IS #560: memoize the FACTS across PROCESSES.  The
walk is pure, and PCL_PROTO_ORACLE's JSON dump already serialises exactly what
_merge_module_prototypes consumes (validated over 95 modules in s412).

GUARD: Pl/t/module-prototype-scan-01.t (8 rows) -- four fixture modules built
in a temp lib, identical but for the package name (Test2::PclGuard,
Test::PclGuard, Test2::Deep::PclGuard, My::PclGuard = the control), each in
both spellings (`blk { 42; }` = the drop, `twice { 21 }` = the silent
mis-parse).  A re-introduced name list fails it whatever names it lists.
Inverse-run with the skip restored: 8/8 fail.
subject: The prototype pre-scan SKIPS every Test2::/Test:: module by name, so a block-form call to a dist-declared (&)-prototyped sub does not parse -- 79 of the 83 drops in the new cpan-t census population, and the no-semicolon spelling is silently mis-parsed instead
